blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it

findings.recommendation: Flatten and name the rules so the function reads without the plan. Skip rows with an empty email with an early `continue` (and say why they are skipped). Extract the duplicated seat loop — it appears once under `Some(account)` and once under `None` — into a helper such as `add_new_seats(db, account_id, seats, existing) -> Result<usize, DbError>`, and replace the bare `seat.contains('@')` by a named predicate (`is_valid_seat_email`) so the reader knows seats that are not emails are dropped on purpose. The condition `account.plan != row.plan` is where a newcomer stumbles: read at this depth, it says that seats are added to an existing account only when its plan differs from the CSV row, and that the plan itself is never updated — nothing tells whether that is the intended rule or an inverted test; give it a name or a comment stating the why (or, if unintended, raise it to the developer). Then the body is one match of two arms, each a call, at most two levels deep.
findings.title: `import` nests six levels deep and hides its seat rules
